designAuthority.acceptanceBranch: GAME-387 AC1 permits a real Figma file/handoff OR an equivalent production design authority. This contract is the 'equivalent production design authority' branch.
designAuthority.whyNotFigma: No Figma integration, credential, or design-tool access is available. docs/DEFINITION_OF_DONE.md section 4 lists 'a real Figma design action (ML-DESIGN)' as a stop condition, and simulating it is explicitly unacceptable. The package was built and the exact pending gate is recorded instead.
designAuthority.whatThisIs: A machine-checked specification of every state GAME-387 names, bound to the identifiers the implementation actually uses, with coverage, design-rule conformance, and honesty enforced by scripts/verify-contracts.mjs.
whatThisIsNot: not a visual design tool file, and therefore not a substitute for one
not human design review, aesthetic approval, or learner-experience sign-off
not evidence that any screen has been seen, used, or judged by a person
not an accessibility conformance claim; docs/ACCESSIBILITY.md section 4 reserves that for ML-16 human evidence
not evidence that any specified screen has been implemented
designAuthority.enforcement: scripts/verify-contracts.mjs fails if a GAME-387 required state is dropped, if a design rule loses its mechanism, if a spec/implementation divergence is undeclared, or if this file claims review that did not happen.
fidelityLimits: No screenshot, wireframe image, or rendered mock exists. Coverage is specified, not depicted.
Typography scale, spacing rhythm, iconography, and final art direction are specified as constraints and tokens; their aesthetic quality is unjudged and belongs to ML-12.
Interaction timing budgets are proposed targets for ML-14 to measure; they are not measurements.
No screen has been reviewed by a designer, a teacher, or a learner.
pendingGates: O-01: owner provides or approves a real Figma file, or waives it in favour of this equivalent
ML-16: human design, classroom, and accessibility review of the screens this contract specifies

authorityLaw.statement: No visual may state a scientific value that differs from authoritative domain state.
rules: every displayed quantity comes from the typed view model, never from pixel geometry
display rounding uses the single frozen round-half-away-from-zero rule and never feeds back into domain state
a vector length, arrow head, or screen position may encode a value only when it is a pure function of that value from the view model
a screen may never display a science value the domain did not emit, and may never interpolate between recorded samples as though they were recorded
decorative physics is permitted only when it is non-authoritative, deterministic, removable under reduced motion, and incapable of changing a science result

designRules.rule: visual vectors and labels must not imply science values inconsistent with authoritative domain state
designRules.mechanism: Force direction is encoded three ways: arrow geometry, the sign of the displacement, and the words in the label. Force magnitude maps linearly from the authoritative net force through a pure function with no frame input. The scene never draws an interpolated position between recorded samples.

designRules.rule: graphs require semantic and table equivalents
designRules.mechanism: Every graph ships with a real table element exposing the same series and values plus a textual summary. No assessed question is answerable from graph geometry alone.

designRules.rule: drag may be an enhancement only
designRules.mechanism: No essential action has a drag-only path. Every drag affordance has a keyboard-reachable discrete equivalent: numeric entry, a stepper, or a range input paired with a readable value.

designRules.rule: essential controls remain semantic DOM controls
designRules.mechanism: Essential actions are real button, input, select, fieldset, and table elements with accessible names. No clickable div and no ARIA-recreated widget carries an essential action. The Phaser canvas is role=img with a label built from the same instrument readings the DOM shows.

Layout, palette, iconography, copy, art, and audio are original. The palette is derived from this repository's own surface tokens. ML-16 performs the originality and IP review; it is not performed here.

tokens.method: Values are transcribed from the shipped custom properties. Contrast ratios are measured, not estimated: WCAG 2.x relative luminance per sRGB pair, then (lighter+0.05)/(darker+0.05).

color.role: input well, table head, canvas bed
secondary text, help text, axis labels
primary action, current step, cart body
force vector, invalid-state cue, fallback border
focus ring only; carries no meaning on its own

measuredContrast.verdict: clears the 3:1 non-text threshold for a UI component boundary (was 1.60:1; remediated as OF-01)
not a supported pairing: nothing places text on the boundary, which is a 1px edge. Kept so the cost of the OF-01 fix stays visible instead of hidden.

focusRing.rationale: outline rather than box-shadow, so the indicator survives forced-colors mode and is not clipped by an element's own overflow.

spacing.rhythm: 0.25rem inside a field, 0.5rem between actions, 1rem panel padding, 1rem panel stack, 1rem section rhythm

typography.numericFigures: font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums is mandatory wherever changing numbers are compared side by side, so digits do not shift horizontally while a trial plays.

canvasType.rationale: The canvas status line prints live values; a monospace face stops the readout reflowing horizontally mid-run.

rendererPalette.method: Contrast measured against the scene background 0x0e1726, which is the same base as --surface.

measuredContrast.name: tick
measuredContrast.verdict: passes non-text 3:1 with headroom; the ruler is the scale encoding, so this is load-bearing (was 3.10:1, remediated with OF-02)

measuredContrast.name: trackEdge
measuredContrast.verdict: clears the 3:1 non-text threshold for a meaningful boundary (was 2.21:1; remediated as OF-02)

measuredContrast.name: track
measuredContrast.verdict: bed fill only, not a meaningful boundary; the ticks and edge carry the scale

measuredContrast.name: progressTrack
measuredContrast.verdict: unfilled rail only; the filled portion is the encoded value

redundantChannels: the words in the force label
the +x axis marker drawn on the laboratory axis
directionEncoding.balancedStateRepresentation: A balanced net force draws NO arrow at all (fromX and toX are null), not a zero-length arrow. A zero-length arrow would read as 'no data' rather than 'a real measured zero'.
directionEncoding.balancedLabelWording: The balanced case states the number as well as the reading: 'balanced (0.0 N)'. The number is the evidence; 'balanced' is the interpretation.

breakpoints.notes: One column, panels stacked in loop order: brief, predict, experiment setup, lab view, instruments, trial record. The lab canvas keeps its 720/320 aspect ratio and its own vertical scroll is avoided; the page scrolls instead.

One column at the same order, with wider measure and larger panel padding. Wider viewports are deliberately not given a second column here so the reading order of the investigation stays top-to-bottom.

Two columns. Left column carries the learner-authored inputs (prediction, experiment setup). Right column carries the observation surface (lab view, instruments). The trial record spans full width beneath both, because a comparison table must never be narrowed into horizontal scrolling.

gridSpecification.css: grid-template-columns: 1fr by default, with @media (min-width: 1024px) overriding to repeat(2, minmax(0, 1fr))
gridSpecification.measuredBehaviour: Two columns begin at exactly 1024px, matching the specified desktop breakpoint. There is no longer an emergent threshold to reconcile.
gridSpecification.resolution: OF-03, remediated in PR #11. The shipped rule was repeat(auto-fit, minmax(320px, 1fr)), which reached two columns at 688px because that threshold was an arithmetic accident of the floor, gap and padding rather than a designed breakpoint. Raising the minmax floor to 488px would have produced exactly 1024px and is the wrong fix: a fixed floor larger than the viewport cannot shrink, so a 320px phone and 200% zoom in a narrow window would overflow horizontally and break the reflow contract. The shipped CSS now declares one column by default and two columns only from a 1024px min-width query, which is what this contract always specified, and the columns use minmax(0, 1fr) so they can shrink below any intrinsic minimum rather than overflowing it. The CSS was changed, not this contract, because the contract was already correct.

reflow.requirement: At 200% zoom and at 320px viewport width, content reflows with no loss of function and no two-dimensional scrolling for text.
prohibited: horizontal scrolling to read a sentence, a label, or a unit
a table that forces the page to scroll sideways to read a value
text under 0.9rem that only exists to make a layout fit
reflow.wideDataHandling: Wide tables scroll inside their own bounded region with a scrollable wrapper and a caption naming the columns, rather than widening the page. The wrapper is focusable so a keyboard user can scroll it, and the full data is always available in the instrument readouts regardless of scroll position.

canvasBox.sizingAuthority: The Phaser Scale Manager owns canvas sizing in FIT mode so the scene's logical coordinate space stays fixed and independent of the screen. CSS must not add a second sizing authority on the same element.
canvasBox.consequence: A viewport change can never change a metre value. Pixels are presentation only and are never read back.

stateCoverage.note: One entry per GAME-387 required state. implementationStatus is the honest current state: implemented means the screen exists in src/, partial means some of the specified states exist, specified means the design is frozen here and the implementing issue has not built it yet.
stateCoverage.phaseReconciliation: docs/PRODUCT.md section 'Session shape' names nine learner steps. src/domain/types.ts MISSION_PHASE_ORDER defines seven authoritative phases. Graph and Claim are stages inside the compare and debrief phases rather than separate authoritative phases, and this contract maps them accordingly.

states.notes: The phase chip list exists; the authored mission brief and its science question do not. They are ML-05 content, presented by ML-10.
One screen or less per docs/PRODUCT.md. Must state the question and the assessed evidence without naming the answer.

textarea plus save, with a role=status confirmation and an explicit invitation to revise the prediction later. Revising after seeing evidence is part of the method, so the copy must never imply a prediction is final.

The domain classifies a change as valid, unchanged, multiple-variables-changed, or controlled-variable-changed and writes learner-facing pedagogy for the invalid cases. The screen that SHOWS the learner which role each variable plays does not exist yet. ML-10 owns it; the design requirement is that the role is stated in words, never by colour alone.

Mass, applied force, and initial velocity are range inputs with paired output readouts; observation window is a number input. Help text states the relationship and the sign convention. Bounds are the declared contract bounds, and the engine clamps rather than trusting the caller.

areas.area: laboratory track, cart, and force presentation

states.notes: Track bed with a metre tick every whole metre, cart body and two wheels, force arrow with an arrowhead, a +x axis marker, a playback rail, and a monospace status line. Geometry is a pure function of the view model with no frame-time input.

areas.area: run, pause, reset, step, and replay

states.authority: usePlayback presentation clock over recorded samples
states.notes: Playing shows the recorded sample at the playback clock. The clock selects which already-computed sample is drawn and cannot change a sample, a measurement, or a result.
The button toggles between Pause and Resume. Paused part-way is distinguished from settled in the scene's own status words, not by colour.

states.authority: reset-session intent; ML-04 allocates a new trial ordinal
states.notes: Reset is non-punitive and must never rewrite recorded history. The spec requires a confirmation whenever recorded trials exist, because a reset that silently discards evidence is a data-loss defect, not a convenience.

states.authority: nextSampleSeconds over the recorded sample instants
states.notes: Step forward and step back move the presentation clock to the next or previous RECORDED sample instant. This is the affordance that keeps the window readable when animation is switched off, so it is required even when reduced motion is off.

Replay re-presents a recorded trial. It must not re-run the domain, must not create a new trial record, and must not alter any measured value. Deterministic replay that re-executes from provenance is a separate ML-04 facility and is a different feature.

Position, velocity, acceleration, net force, and elapsed time as a description list, plus the derived ML-04 measurements. Every reading carries value, displayValue, text, unit, and origin. Configured values are marked configured and measured values measured so a learner can tell what they set from what happened.
Arrow length is base plus a fixed pixel count per newton, capped at the largest force the frozen range allows. Direction is stated in words beside it. A balanced net force draws no arrow.

A real table with a caption, column headers, and row headers exists and shows configuration and final values. It does not yet show provenance, measurements, the integrity digest, or the changed-versus-controlled analysis that ML-08 owns.

The notebook is the ordered, append-only list of trials with each trial's role, its configuration, its measurements, and whether it is admissible for a claim. Design requirement: a learner must be able to see at a glance which variable changed between two entries and which were held fixed.

A real comparison table over two or more trials. Each column is a trial, each row a variable, and the independent variable's cells are marked as the changed one. Invalid comparisons are labelled in words, naming the count of changed variables or the controlled variable that moved, and never by colour alone.
Curvature indicates greater acceleration. Used optionally in cargo-load-test and never as the only route to the data.

Slope is the acceleration. Required by thruster-test and mystery-cart, which is what discharges the Epic's graph-interpretation requirement. Mystery-cart requires a two-trace overlay to compare slopes.

The learner states a claim about a named measurement, the direction of the relationship, and the variable that explains it. The design must require all three parts rather than accepting free text alone, because a claim that names no variable cannot be wrong in a way the debrief can correct.
Trials are cited by checkbox over the notebook. Only replayable evidence is admissible. Inadmissible citations are refused with a stated reason rather than silently dropped.
Authored explanation, misconception feedback that points at the learner's own recorded numbers, and a non-punitive revision path. Never a score, a timer, or an answer key.
Hints nudge toward the method, never name the answer. Retry is unlimited or clearly bounded and non-punitive, and allocates a new trial ordinal rather than overwriting one.

Renderer recovery is per failure stage. A chunk-load failure offers a page reload, because the browser remembers a failed dynamic import for the life of the page; every other stage retries in place. The reload warns first that trial records are not stored, so the session starts fresh.

The ErrorBoundary renders role=alert. Validation errors have typed codes and learner-facing explanations. Field-level invalid states, their text, and their announcement are specified here and are not yet built.
The region states that the animated view is starting and that every number below is available as text, so a slow renderer is never read as a broken page.

A dashed, non-colour-only panel names the failure stage, gives the reason, states that nothing about the experiment changed, and offers the correct recovery for that stage. The semantic instruments and trial table remain available throughout.

controlStates.requiredBy: GAME-387 required design coverage: keyboard focus, selected, disabled, error, non-color, and reduced-motion states

states.specification: Surface-raised panels sit on surface with a 1px border and 10px radius. Primary actions are an accent fill with accent-ink text at 8px radius. Secondary actions are transparent with a border and ink text. Inputs are surface-sunken wells with a border, 6px radius, and 0.45rem padding.
A visible fill or border change on pointer hover. Never the only affordance: hover must not be what makes a control discoverable.

A 3px solid --focus outline with a 2px offset and 4px radius, applied through :focus-visible. It must never be suppressed, and no element may set outline: none without an equally visible replacement. Because it is an outline rather than a box-shadow it is not clipped by an ancestor's overflow and it survives forced-colors mode.
states.rationale: docs/ACCESSIBILITY.md requires a visible focus indicator at high contrast in every theme. The measured contrast of --focus against both surfaces is 12.46 and 10.81.

states.specification: Selected is encoded by at least two of an accent fill, a weight increase, an explicit textual marker, and a shape change. The current mission step is the only selected state shipped today, and it combines an accent fill with bold weight and aria-current=step. Trial selection and evidence citation must additionally carry a visible textual marker such as the word selected or a named check glyph, because a control that relies on fill alone is a colour-only distinction.
states.implementedIn: src/app/styles.css .phase-list li[aria-current=step]; trial and evidence selection are specified only

appliesTo: playback controls before a trial exists
states.specification: opacity 0.55 with cursor not-allowed. A disabled control is also non-focusable, so every disabled control must be paired with visible help text explaining what will enable it. The playback controls are disabled until a trial exists, and the design requires the panel to say why rather than presenting inert buttons.
states.implementedIn: src/app/styles.css button:disabled; the reason is now stated in static text in src/ui/InstrumentPanel.tsx and covered by a browser test, remediated as OF-04

states.specification: An error is stated in words, adjacent to the offending control, associated by aria-describedby, and announced through a live region. Colour is a redundant third channel only. The renderer fallback additionally uses a dashed border as well as the --warn colour. Every rejection branch in the domain already carries learner-facing copy, so no rejection is silent.
states.implementedIn: src/app/ErrorBoundary.tsx and src/domain/variables.ts carry the copy; field-level error presentation is specified only

states.specification: Direction, state, selection, validity, comparison series, and force magnitude each carry a redundant non-colour channel. Force direction uses an arrowhead plus words plus sign. The ruler uses labelled ticks. The current step uses weight plus fill plus aria-current. Validity uses wording. Graph series use line style plus a direct label plus a row in the table.
states.implementedIn: src/renderer/labScene.ts, src/ui/InstrumentPanel.tsx, src/viewmodel/instruments.ts; graph series styling is specified only

states.specification: Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, playback does not animate and resolves to the end of the recorded window in one step; the panel states that reduced motion is on and names Step forward, Step back, and Jump to end as the way through the window; all CSS animation and transition durations collapse to 0.001ms with a single iteration; smooth scrolling is disabled. Instructional meaning is unchanged: every value reachable by watching is reachable by stepping.
states.implementedIn: src/app/styles.css reduced-motion block, src/host/usePrefersReducedMotion.ts, src/ui/InstrumentPanel.tsx reduced-motion note, src/renderer/labGeometry.ts emphasis settled

states.specification: Nothing may rely on a background image or a subtle border to convey state, because forced-colors mode replaces both. System colour keywords and border-based indicators must survive.
states.implementedIn: src/app/styles.css forced-colors: active block, added as OF-06 remediation; not yet observed in a real forced-colors browser, which remains ML-16's manual gate
states.rationale: Named because the focus ring's outline-based choice was made for this case, so the same reasoning should reach the other indicators.

states.specification: Reflow with no loss of function and no two-dimensional scrolling for text. Layout is built on a single-column-first auto-fit grid so reflow is inherent rather than patched.
states.implementedIn: src/app/styles.css .app__grid; reflow has not been manually qualified at 200% zoom

focusOrder.rule: DOM order is reading order. Focus is never trapped except in a deliberate modal, which returns focus on close.

announcements.canvasStatus: role=img with an aria-label built from the same instrument readings the visible readouts use, so a screen-reader user and a sighted user can never be told different values.
announcements.rule: No live region may report a state that differs only in wording from a visual state, and none may update more than once per recorded sample.

principles: authoritative samples only; a graph never interpolates between samples as though the intermediate instants were recorded
deterministic domain and scale selection, so the same evidence always draws the same graph
labelled axes carrying SI units, with the unit in the axis title rather than left to convention
an explicit origin, and a truncated axis is never used when truncation would change the interpretation
a real table equivalent exposing the same series and the same values, plus a textual summary
a keyboard-reachable read-value-at-time affordance, so the graph can be interrogated without a pointer

series.curvatureMeaning: not meaningful in v1, where acceleration is constant within a segment
series.zeroReferenceMeaning: a horizontal trace at zero velocity; a rising line above zero and one below zero must be visually and verbally distinct

seriesEncoding.rule: Each trial is a series. Series are distinguished by line style plus a direct label on the trace plus a row in the table, never by colour alone.
seriesEncoding.overlayRule: Mystery Cart requires at least one variant overlaying two velocity-time traces to compare slopes. The overlay must name both trials and state which slope is larger in words.

states.specification: States that no trial has been recorded yet and what to do, rather than drawing an empty axis that reads like a zero measurement.
One labelled trace with axis titles and units.
Two or more labelled traces, each directly labelled, with a legend also available as text.
A keyboard-reachable control that reports the value of each series at a chosen time, using the same formatter as the rest of the product.
A real table with a caption and scoped headers holding every plotted value.
One sentence stating the relationship the graph shows, in words, with slope or curvature never the only access path.
States that the recorded trials cannot support the comparison yet and which trial is missing.

prohibited: a graph drawn from pixel or sprite positions
smoothed, splined, or otherwise fitted data presented as recorded
a truncated axis presented without an explicit break marker
a graph as the only route to a value required for a claim

motionContract.principle: Instructional visualization and decorative polish are different categories with different rules. They are separated here so ML-12 polish can never quietly become load-bearing.

categories.definition: Motion that carries scientific or procedural meaning a learner needs.
rules: a non-motion equivalent must exist and must be reachable by keyboard
it may not be the only route to any value, relationship, or state change
it must be removable under prefers-reduced-motion with meaning preserved
it must be driven by recorded sample instants, never by frame time
it must not pace the investigation: no next step is gated on an animation finishing

inventory.meaning: position changes with time under the authoritative trace
inventory.nonMotionEquivalent: Step forward and Step back through recorded samples, and the trial table's final values
inventory.reducedMotionBehaviour: resolve to the end of the window in one step
inventory.currentImplementation: the scene redraws the same picture for the same model; the presentation clock selects which recorded sample is shown

inventory.nonMotionEquivalent: the force label in words beside the arrow, and the Net force instrument readout
inventory.reducedMotionBehaviour: arrow drawn statically at full length; never grown or faded
inventory.currentImplementation: the arrow is present or absent from the first frame and never animates

inventory.meaning: how far through the recorded window the presentation clock is
inventory.nonMotionEquivalent: the elapsed-time instrument reading, which is the recorded sample's own time
inventory.reducedMotionBehaviour: the rail jumps to the end
inventory.currentImplementation: playedFraction is derived from the model's active index and cannot move a measurement

inventory.nonMotionEquivalent: the new row in the trial table and the status announcement

categories.definition: Motion that adds nothing scientific and exists only for feel.
rules: removable under prefers-reduced-motion with zero meaning loss
non-authoritative and incapable of changing a science result
deterministic where it can affect what is on screen at all
must not delay any action or gate any next step

inventory.status: exists as a CSS rule; no bespoke transitions authored yet
prohibited as specified; non-authoritative idle animation is not authorised in v1
not built; if authored it may never read as a score or a reward

categories.definition: Anything that would make the renderer an authority for a science value.
rules: a tween, easing curve, or interpolation that positions the cart between recorded samples as though the intermediate instants were recorded
a sprite position or collision outcome used as a measurement
a frame counter or elapsed frame time used to advance, ease, or drift the picture
any animation whose completion changes domain state
categories.currentImplementation: enforced: src/renderer/labScene.ts reads no frame time, uses no tween, and computes all geometry through sceneGeometry, which is a pure function of the view model
categories.verification: tests/unit/labGeometry.test.ts and tests/e2e/realRender.spec.ts assert the drawn geometry matches the pure function across advancing frames and viewport sizes

timing.status: targets proposed here for ML-14 to measure; they are not measurements and no gate is claimed
timing.stateChangeFeedback: visible within 100ms of a committed action
timing.playbackStep: one recorded sample per activation, with no transition between steps
timing.prohibited: any deliberate dwell that blocks the next trial; scorecard row Q-10 forbids an animation dwell gating the next trial

assetDirection.originalityPosition: All Motion Lab art, iconography, typography choices, and audio are original work, derived from this repository's own token set and from the physics the kernel computes. No comparator art, layout, name, copy, audio, or scene composition may be reproduced (docs/COMPARATORS.md IP boundary).
assetDirection.paletteLock: The palette is fixed by this contract's tokens and rendererPalette sections. ML-12 may not introduce a new hue for a scientific distinction; a new meaning requires a decision entry.
direction: Laboratory instrumentation rather than a cartoon world: a readable apparatus, honest instrument faces, and a clear track, in the spirit of a real test bench.
Physics-driven visuals only. Cart, arrow, ruler, and trace are generated from the frozen model, so art and science cannot drift apart.
Instrument typography is monospace with tabular figures wherever numbers change during playback.
One idea per screen: the learner always knows which single thing this panel is for.
Restraint over spectacle. ML-12 polish may not add a visual that implies a science value the domain did not emit.

assetProvenance.rule: Every nontrivial shipped asset records assetId, path, kind, origin, author or tool, license, sourceUrl, derivedFrom, and notes, exactly as docs/PROVENANCE.md section 2 specifies.
assetProvenance.status: no production asset exists; the asset manifest is not authored, and no asset may ship until it is

iconography.specification: Direction and state glyphs are single-weight, drawn from one grid, and always paired with a text label. An icon is never the only carrier of meaning, and an icon implying a science value must come from the model.
iconography.currentImplementation: the force direction glyph in src/ui/InstrumentPanel.tsx is a text arrow character paired with the words in the label

assetDirection.reviewStatus: direction documented here; the originality and IP review is ML-16's gate and has not occurred

criteria.criterion: A real Figma file/handoff or equivalent production design authority is recorded.
criteria.honestQualifier: No Figma file was produced and none is claimed. AC1's equivalent-production-design-authority branch is taken. O-01 remains owner-gated: the owner must still provide or approve a real Figma file, or waive it in favour of this.

criteria.criterion: All ML-11 vertical-slice states are covered before ML-11 begins.
criteria.honestQualifier: Every ML-11 state is specified. Specifying a state is not implementing it, and ML-11 stays blocked by GAME-394 in the Jira blocker chain regardless.

criteria.criterion: Responsive and accessibility variants are explicit, not left to implementation guesswork.
criteria.honestQualifier: Variants are explicit, including measured contrast and one declared divergence from the shipped grid. Human review of those variants has not occurred.

criteria.criterion: Motion specs distinguish instructional visualization from decorative polish.
criteria.honestQualifier: Three categories are separated, with a non-motion equivalent named for every instructional motion and a forbidden category for anything that would make the renderer an authority.
Direction and the IP boundary are documented. No asset exists, no manifest is authored, and the ML-16 originality review has not occurred.

ml11Traceability.note: GAME-395's vertical slice must run mission question, prediction, controlled setup, animated real Phaser run, measurement, immutable trial record, second trial, graph, comparison, claim, evidence, and explanatory debrief. Each step maps to a state specified here and to the issue that must implement it.
ml11Traceability.honestyStatement: Coverage is complete; implementation is not. Six of the twelve steps are unimplemented or partial, and GAME-395 is blocked by GAME-394 in any case. This contract does not make ML-11 achievable.

openFindings.policy: Recorded as open, never as passes. An unresolved finding here is not a defect in this contract; it is work the contract identified and assigned.

findings.finding: No visual design artifact exists. Coverage is specified rather than depicted, so composition, hierarchy, and aesthetic quality are unjudged.
findings.action: The owner provides or approves a real Figma file under O-01, or waives it explicitly. Human design review is ML-16's gate.

resolvedFindings.policy: Findings closed by a later change, kept so the record shows what the defect actually was rather than leaving no trace of something that was once real. A resolved finding is never counted as evidence that it never existed. Each entry declares manualGate: a fix that still needs human qualification must name it, and a fix that does not may not.

findings.was: --border on --surface-raised measured 1.60:1, below the 3:1 WCAG 1.4.11 non-text contrast for a UI component boundary.
findings.resolution: Raised by a uniform channel scale of 1.65 so hue and relative saturation are unchanged. A free search for any passing colour returned saturated blues such as #204cff, which would have cleared the ratio and wrecked the palette's muted character; a hue-preserving scale is the smaller and more defensible change.
findings.cost: --ink on --border falls from 8.47:1 to 4.27:1. Nothing places text on the boundary, and the pairing is recorded explicitly so the cost stays visible.

findings.was: The scene track edge measured 2.21:1 against the scene background, below the 3:1 non-text contrast for a meaningful boundary.
findings.now: trackEdge is 0x45689f and measures 3.19:1 against the scene background.
findings.resolution: Raised by a uniform channel scale of 1.30, so hue is unchanged. tick was raised alongside it to 0x5a7dad at 4.25:1 for two reasons: raising the edge alone would have inverted the hierarchy so the bed outline outranked the ruler, and the tick is the load-bearing scale encoding this contract had already flagged as sitting barely over the threshold at 3.10:1.

findings.was: The shipped auto-fit grid reached two columns at 688px while this contract specifies the desktop two-column layout from 1024px.
findings.now: The shipped grid declares one column by default and two columns only from a 1024px min-width query.
findings.resolution: The shipped CSS was changed, not this contract, because the 688px threshold was an arithmetic accident of a 320px floor plus a 16px gap plus 32px of padding, never a designed breakpoint, so the contract was already correct. Raising the minmax floor to 488px would have hit 1024px exactly but would have broken reflow: a fixed floor larger than the viewport cannot shrink, so a 320px phone and 200% zoom would overflow horizontally.

findings.was: Disabled playback controls gave no visible reason for being disabled before a trial exists.
findings.now: The instrument panel states, in always-present text, that playback is unavailable until a trial has been recorded and names Run preview as the action that enables it.
findings.resolution: A disabled control is not focusable, so an unexplained disabled button is never encountered by a keyboard or screen-reader user. The reason therefore lives in static text rather than a hover tooltip, and it names the enabling action rather than only apologising. Covered by a new browser test in tests/e2e/accessibility.spec.ts.

findings.was: The forced-colors state was specified but unimplemented, and no indicator had been qualified in forced-colors mode.
findings.now: src/app/styles.css carries a forced-colors: active block that re-expresses every indicator as a system colour or a border.
findings.resolution: The product already carried every distinction redundantly, so nothing had to be invented. What the block prevents is the browser's own substitutions deleting a cue: forced-colors mode replaces background colours and box-shadows, so a state expressed only by a fill would disappear. Panel, control, table, chip, disabled and fallback boundaries are all restated as borders or system colours, and the focus ring is restated against Highlight.
findings.stillPending: No indicator has been observed in a real forced-colors browser. Manual qualification is ML-16's gate and has not happened; implementing the CSS is not qualifying it.

changeLog.change: Version 1.1.0. Both measured non-text contrast failures fixed by hue-preserving uniform channel scaling: --border from 1.60:1 to 3.17:1 and the scene trackEdge from 2.21:1 to 3.19:1, with the load-bearing ruler tick raised to 4.25:1 to preserve the visual hierarchy. The 688px versus 1024px grid divergence fixed in the shipped CSS rather than in this contract, because the threshold was an arithmetic accident rather than a design decision, and via a min-width query rather than a raised floor so narrow viewports cannot overflow. Disabled playback controls now state their reason in static text covered by a browser test, and a forced-colors block re-expresses every indicator as a system colour or border. OF-01 through OF-04 and OF-06 move to resolvedFindings with their was, now and resolution; OF-05 and OF-07 remain open. Every contrast ratio and the two-column breakpoint are recomputed from the shipped sources by the verifier, so none of these numbers is trusted text.

changeLog.change: Version 1.1.1. OF-07 moves from openFindings to resolvedFindings: the different-model independent review of PR #11 is recorded in GAME-387 comment 15634, and the owner approved the O-01 equivalent design-authority branch in comment 15640. OF-05 remains open and is the single recorded design limitation, because no visual design artifact exists. OF-01 and OF-02 gain nowMeasurements, so the ratios quoted in their now text are recomputed from the shipped tokens and renderer palette instead of trusted; a resolved finding that quotes a ratio in its now without a matching recomputed measurement now fails the gate. This corrects the sentence in the 1.1.0 entry below, which claimed that every contrast ratio is recomputed: that was true of the measured contrast tables and the renderer palette, but not of ratios quoted in prose, and the claim is corrected here rather than left standing. Two gate holes are closed: the base-grid floor check now asserts the track sizing shape instead of the absence of a px/rem token, so minmax(20em, 1fr) can no longer reintroduce the cannot-shrink overflow trap; and the forced-colors checks are scoped to the forced-colors block with CSS comments stripped, so a comment naming a system colour can no longer satisfy a check whose rule was deleted, and the disabled-control rule must carry opacity: 1 explicitly. Two doc corrections: the duplicate 4.2 heading in docs/DESIGN.md is renumbered, and the openFindings key regains its two-space indent. No token, palette, breakpoint, state, control state, or design decision changed, and nothing here alters what the design says.
